title: Early severe skin disease with normal glucose
summary: An eight-year-old boy had skin laxity at birth. From about age two, progressive hyperpigmented velvety thickening began in skin folds and became generalised. He has sparse curly hair, numerous skin tags, mild cognitive impairment, developmental delay, enamel erosion and low bone mineral density. No similar skin disorder is reported in the family.

case.initial_facts:
An eight-year-old boy had skin laxity at birth. From about age two, progressive hyperpigmented velvety thickening began in skin folds and became generalised. He has sparse curly hair, numerous skin tags, mild cognitive impairment, developmental delay, enamel erosion and low bone mineral density. No similar skin disorder is reported in the family.
Glucose status is described as normal. A popliteal skin biopsy shows hyperkeratosis, papillomatosis and acanthosis without an inflammatory infiltrate. Molecular results, chest imaging and treatment response have not been supplied.

case.hidden: The source later identifies a de novo germline EGFR L858R variant in patient 2, with pulmonary nodules found after molecular investigation and improvement during targeted treatment. Patient 3 has a different mosaic distribution; patient 1 has different age, comorbidity and lung pathology.
case.reference: Integrate early-onset severe generalised skin findings with associated developmental and other features rather than treating normal glucose as proof that no relevant disease exists. A syndromic/genetic assessment and review for systemic involvement are defensible. Negative reported family history does not exclude a de novo disorder. Molecular cause, systemic investigation results and treatment response remain unknown. Keep the supplied individual separate from other patients.
